topic: Can oblique projection in beam coverage impact inter-cell interference differently than orthographic projection in GEO satellites?
consensus_response: Oblique projection mixed with ellipse projection in multibeam satellite systems introduces deviations between satellite terminals and cell centers, affecting interference strength. Unlike orthographic projection in GEO satellites, oblique projection's angular selectivity is harder to idealize, introducing co-channel interference among adjacent spot beams. The satellite antenna acts as a spatial filter, exacerbating inter-cell interference. Phased array antenna errors further complicate the system, requiring sophisticated resource allocation and beamforming techniques to mitigate co-channel interference. The Earth's rotation affects the accuracy of oblique projection, introducing additional deviations between user positions and cell centers.
reference_context: Multibeam satellite systems use a combination of oblique and ellipse projections, which leads to differences in inter-cell interference compared to traditional cellular distribution. The deviation angle between satellite terminals and cell centers affects interference strength, making it challenging to maintain perfect orthogonality between cells.
